## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Anopamātherīgāthā* (Thig 6.5) is a Pali verse text in the *Therīgāthā* collection of the Sutta Piṭaka [SuttaCentral]. The verses represent the spiritual testimony of the elder nun (*therī*) Anopamā. In modern scholarship on the ordination and early history of the *bhikkhunīsaṅgha*, Anopamā's verses are cited among the testimonies of prominent early Buddhist women renunciants [Appleton, Buddha as Storyteller]. Drawing on the traditional commentary, scholars observe that Anopamā was among the rare female practitioners recorded as having attained the fruition of a non-returner (*anāgāmin*) before taking formal monastic ordination [Karma Sonam Palmo].

SuttaCentral indexes sixteen modern translations across eleven languages, including English translations by Ayya Soma and Bhikkhu Sujato [SuttaCentral].

Regarding parallels and textual reuse, SuttaCentral records no curated parallels, and DharmaNexus identifies no cross-language matches meeting its threshold in Chinese, Sanskrit, or Tibetan corpora [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. Within the Pali tradition, DharmaNexus identifies four matching segments (664 characters) between the verses and the *Therīgāthā-aṭṭhakathā* (Paramatthadīpanī VI), showing that the verses (specifically segments §0.3–7.1) are quoted and commented upon in commentary sections §2136–2152 [DharmaNexus].
